minutes.headline: Selectmen opened the annual town meeting warrant and pressed for a joint meeting on school building contingency spending.
minutes.summary: Board members debated whether items the school building committee is considering, such as signage and touchscreen wiring, belong in the project contingency, and asked for an agenda item and a joint meeting. A resident and a companion asked the board to look at paratransit service reaching a mobile home park, and a resident volunteered rides. The board opened the warrant, renewed an entertainment license, reviewed a license fee survey, and went into executive session.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted to open the annual town meeting warrant and set it to close on March 24 at 6pm.
Members questioned whether items such as signage and touchscreens belong in the school building contingency, and agreed to schedule a future agenda item, possibly a joint meeting.
A resident asked the board to look at paratransit service to a mobile home park; the MART representative will follow up and take his contact information.
Staff will add a column of licenses issued per category to the license fee survey, which members noted shows the town below average on many fees.
A motion to renew the weekday entertainment license for the Bootlegger was made, but the result is not audible in the recording.

why_it_matters: Items added to the school building project and paid from its contingency fall on local taxpayers unless the state reimburses them, so the joint meeting is where that question gets answered.
The warrant sets the articles voters will be asked to act on at town meeting, and the license fee survey could lead to fee changes for local businesses.
